en: Jose Rizal annotated a 1609 history book to prove Filipinos had a rich culture before Spanish colonization.
The Philippine tarsier has individual eyes that are as large as its entire brain, allowing it to see in the dark.
The Philippine Supreme Court has exactly fifteen justices who sit en banc to decide the most important cases.
The ancient Ibaloi people created Kabayan mummies by slowly dehydrating the dead using a strict herbal smoking process.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator.
The ancient Baybayin script was written on bamboo and leaves, and every single syllable ended in a vowel.
During the Pahiyas Festival, Lucban residents decorate their house exteriors with colorful kipings, which are leaf-shaped rice wafers.
The Philippine Declaration of Independence was written in Spanish by Ambrosio Rianzares Bautista and read aloud on June 12, 1898.
The South Sea Pearl, declared the national gem, is harvested from the giant Pinctada maxima oyster in Philippine waters.
Juan Luna’s famous painting Spoliarium won the first gold medal at the Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts in 1884.
The tradition of bayanihan originally involved an entire community physically carrying a traditional nipa hut to a new location.
The Sangguniang Kabataan allows elected Filipino youth leaders, aged fifteen to thirty, to manage local youth development programs.
